title: Why do biscuits have holes?
caption:
Those tiny holes in your biscuit aren't just design 🍪
Dough has water. In the oven it turns into steam. With no holes, the steam gets trapped — the biscuit puffs up like a balloon and cracks.
The holes let the steam escape, so it bakes flat and crisp. Bakers call it "docking".
